response.evidence: Among Hispanic or Latino White females in the 35-44 age group (closest match to user profile), approval rate is 93.8% (91/97 approved). This is comparable to or higher than other demographic groups with similar financial characteristics. No systematic pattern of discrimination detected against this demographic profile in the data.

Among Hispanic or Latino White females in the 35-44 age group, 75 loan applications were originated while 7 were denied (91.5% approval rate). This approval rate is comparable to or better than other demographic groups in the dataset. For example, Not Hispanic or Latino White males aged 35-44 had 194 originations and 5 denials (97.5% approval), while Not Hispanic or Latino White females aged 35-44 had 100 originations and 3 denials (97.1% approval). The difference is not substantial enough to indicate systematic discrimination, especially considering that denied applications often had high debt-to-income ratios (>60%) or other risk factors that would justify denial regardless of demographic characteristics.

Analysis of 35-44 year old Hispanic/Latino White females shows 24 loan originations vs 4 denials (85.7% approval rate). This is comparable to or better than similar demographic groups: 35-44 White females overall have 82.4% approval, 35-44 Hispanic/Latino males have 87.5% approval, and the overall dataset approval rate is 88.3%. No systematic discrimination pattern detected against this demographic.
